title: Refresh the published Board in place

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-430#refresh-published-board-in-place at 7dcc16adbe3edde4d44d91ee94f3f3a2afa7a497

Verdict: Caught. On the warm-open-after-restart path (and, separately, on the warm Refresh path), maintained assertions failed because the fault made the Board fetch.

Promise: key example "Given a confirmation at A and a restarted dashboard, open the Board. It shows A's revision once origin still advertises A, without fetching." Scope: "An open with a confirmation at origin's advertised revision also skips the fetch." To pass, the open has to answer the recorded revision with a later confirmation time, and the only upload-pack it causes is origin's probe.

Fault: dashboard/server/verifiedOriginTrunk.ts, the warm-path guard changed from
  `former?.revision === probed ? await backlogAt(check, probed) : undefined`
to
  `false && former?.revision === probed ? await backlogAt(check, probed) : undefined`
After this change every check fetches, even when the durable confirmation matches origin's advertised revision. No fixtures or assertions were changed. The caller's suggested fault and both suggested checks held at this revision and were used without changes.

Maintained checks examined:
- dashboard/backend-tests/review/board-confirmation.spec.ts:103, "an open whose record matches origin confirms a later time without fetching, after a restart". Each `restarted()` builds a fresh `verifiedOriginTrunk` with its own PinnedTexts over the same durable record. Upload-packs are counted through a wrapper in `countedUploadPacks`. The first restarted open records B. The second restarted open must answer B with a later time and add exactly one upload-pack.
- e2e/observation/board-refresh-unchanged.spec.ts:38, "Refresh of an unchanged Board advances its confirmation time without fetching". It asserts `transfers.held()` is 1.

Run observations (scratch worktree from a detached checkout at the revision, after `npm ci`, Node 24.21.0):
- Baseline. Backend, board-confirmation.spec.ts: 2 of 2 selected tests passed (proof record phase "completed", selectedCount 2). E2E, board-refresh-unchanged.spec.ts: 1 of 1 selected test passed.
- Faulted backend. The case at :103 failed at line 113, `expect(board.uploadPacks()).toBe(probeOnly)`: expected 3, received 4. Its earlier assertions passed: the answer was B, and the confirmation time was later. The case at :78 still passed; every check in it fetches anyway, so it never reaches the warm branch.
- Faulted E2E. The test failed at line 68, `expect(transfers.held()).toBe(1)`: expected 1, received 2. The steps before it passed: the Board showed A with a later time.
- Independent wrong-behavior witness: GIT_TRACE on the backend spec file. Restored code ran 5 board-ref fetches (`git fetch ... origin +refs/heads/main:refs/open-dough/board/main`). The faulted code ran 6. The extra fetch is the warm restarted open: case :78 fetches on all 4 of its opens either way, and case :103 goes from 1 fetch to 2. GIT_TRACE on the E2E spec showed the same thing: 1 board-ref fetch restored, 2 faulted. So the wrong behavior (fetching on a warm open) actually happened on the path each assertion covers, and was not merely inferred from the assertion's own counter.
- Restoration. An EXIT/INT/TERM trap restored the file with `git checkout`. Afterwards `git status --short` was empty and `git diff --quiet HEAD` passed, at HEAD 7dcc16adb. The scratch checkout was clean before the probe, so no earlier changes needed preserving. After restoring, the backend spec passed 2 of 2 and the E2E spec passed 1 of 1, with proof records "completed" and all tests passed. The scratch worktree was then removed (`git worktree remove --force`).

Assertions that caught the fault:
- board-confirmation.spec.ts:113 (upload-pack count equals probe only), on the backend's restarted-open path.
- board-refresh-unchanged.spec.ts:68 (held transfers equals 1), on the browser's warm Refresh path.
Both claims cover only these observed paths. The backend case confirms the record at B and then reopens at B. That matches the key example's "confirmation at A, origin still at A" with B as the confirmed revision.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise. Both maintained assertions catch the fault on the paths they exercise.

Already-planned repair or prior disposition: none matched. The probe did not lead to any new repair decision.

Cost:
- Test runtime (measured, test runner's own figures). Backend spec: Vitest reported 15.12 s for the baseline, about 1.4 s and 3.4 s per case under the fault, and 2.5 s plus 1.0 s per case restored. E2E spec: Playwright attempt durations were 7.3 s baseline, 8.8 s faulted and 6.3 s restored. Wall time per run was 8–28 s. Host load average was about 30–33 throughout.
- Human effort: unavailable. No separate human measure was recorded; the run was fully delegated.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported measure of tokens or turns is available to this agent.
- Invocation-to-report elapsed: 283143 ms (measured), from 1795783159022 to 1795783442165 in Unix epoch ms.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision 7dcc16adbe3edde4d44d91ee94f3f3a2afa7a497; verdict Caught; no follow-up.
